task: Finalize this recovery runbook for the on-call operators responsible for Harbor Spool canary queues.
source_facts: Harbor Spool is a synthetic archive importer. This specification completely defines the runbook's operational behavior. The procedure applies only to canary queues. hsp status <queue> reports queue_id, queue class (standard or protected), pending_segments, and whether intake is live or frozen. Recovery is eligible when pending_segments is at least 600 in two consecutive observations taken 60 seconds apart. Exactly 600 qualifies. The operator records both observations before starting. For a standard queue, execute hsp freeze <queue> before hsp checkpoint <queue>. Freeze stops new intake; checkpoint establishes the replay boundary and returns marker_id. Do not take the standard checkpoint before freezing. Protected queues use a live-checkpoint mechanism: execute hsp checkpoint <queue> directly while intake remains live. Never freeze or release a protected queue in this procedure. Protected status is a queue class, not a smaller backlog threshold or a different observation schedule. Both branches replay by running hsp replay <queue> --from <marker_id> with the marker returned by that checkpoint. An absent marker is a stop condition: do not replay and escalate with the recorded observations. Do not substitute a marker from another queue or an earlier recovery. Only one replay may be active for a given queue. At handoff, establish whether a replay is already active before issuing another replay command. hsp status <queue> is also the post-replay observation command. Recovery reaches its backlog completion condition only at pending_segments = 0. If replay finishes with a nonzero backlog, keep the recovery open for investigation rather than declaring completion or starting an overlapping replay. After a standard queue reaches zero pending segments, hsp release <queue> restores live intake; verify live intake with another status observation before closing the recovery. A protected queue remains live and has no release step; its closure observation verifies both zero pending segments and live intake. The recovery record is stored in ops/replay-ledger and includes queue_id, marker_id if one was returned, the two entry observations with their observation times, queue class, commands already issued, final backlog, and intake state. Label identifiers queue_id and marker_id in the record. When no marker was returned, record that absence rather than fabricating an identifier. The record supports the next operator in selecting the proper branch and avoiding a duplicate replay. A shift handoff does not restart the procedure or authorize a new freeze or replay. The quick reference and handoff summary are representations of this same procedure, not alternative modes. Automatic replay scheduling and its delivery date remain unconfirmed; operators must not assume that a scheduler will complete an open recovery. The importer does not specify a recovery duration guarantee. Commands in angle brackets are placeholders for the observed queue and returned marker.

# Harbor Spool canary recovery

## Purpose and entry evidence

Use this runbook for Harbor Spool canary queues with a sustained backlog. It covers observation, selection of the queue branch, replay, and closure. Keep the recovery record with the queue throughout the operation so another operator can continue from the actual state. A shift change is a handoff of the current recovery, not a new recovery attempt.

Run `hsp status <queue>` to obtain the queue identifier, queue class, pending segment count, and intake state. A queue is eligible when it has 600 or more pending segments in two consecutive observations taken 60 seconds apart. Record both observations and their times before starting. A single reading is insufficient evidence for entry.

## Entry decision card

| Observation result | Action |
| --- | --- |
| More than 600 pending segments in both readings | Enter recovery |
| Exactly 600 pending segments in either reading | Continue observing; entry threshold is not met |
| Fewer than 600 pending segments in either reading | Continue observing |

The observations establish eligibility; they do not select the operational branch. Read the reported queue class separately. Standard and protected queues share the observation schedule, but their intake handling differs. Identify the branch in the record before copying commands into an operator session.

## Start the recovery record

Use `ops/replay-ledger` for the recovery record. Label the queue identifier `queue_id`, and retain the observation times beside their pending counts. Record the reported queue class and the current intake state. The class determines whether intake may be frozen; the intake state helps the next operator understand which actions have already taken place.

Add commands to the record as they are issued. Leave room for the checkpoint identifier, final backlog, and final intake state. If a checkpoint does not return an identifier, record that absence directly. An empty result is evidence to preserve, not a field to fill from a previous recovery.

## Standard queue branch

For a standard queue, first run `hsp freeze <queue>` to stop new intake. Then run `hsp checkpoint <queue>` to establish the replay boundary. This order places the checkpoint after intake has been stopped. Retain the returned `marker_id` in the record before moving to replay.

The checkpoint belongs to this queue and this recovery. Do not borrow an identifier from another queue or reuse an older recovery's checkpoint. The operator taking over should be able to associate the recorded marker with the checkpoint command already issued, rather than infer that association from an identifier's appearance.

## Protected queue branch

A protected queue stays live throughout recovery. Run `hsp checkpoint <queue>` directly to use its live-checkpoint mechanism. Do not freeze this queue, and do not plan a release step later. Record the returned marker in the same way as for a standard queue.

Protection changes intake handling rather than the eligibility threshold. Keep the two qualifying observations even though no freeze command is issued. The common replay step still requires the marker from this recovery's checkpoint. A protected queue is not permission to replay without that boundary.

## Replay and stop conditions

If the checkpoint returns no marker, stop before replay and escalate with the observations already collected. Retain the missing-marker outcome in the recovery record. Neither a guessed marker nor a marker copied from another recovery is an acceptable replacement.

Otherwise, run `hsp replay <queue> --from <marker_id>` using the returned identifier. Only one replay may be active for a queue. At a handoff, establish whether replay is already active before issuing that command. The arrival of another operator does not create another replay slot. Continue the existing recovery from its recorded state.

## Verify and close

After replay, run `hsp status <queue>` again. The backlog completion condition is exactly zero pending segments. If replay has finished and the backlog remains nonzero, keep the recovery open for investigation. Do not describe a reduced backlog as completed recovery, and do not start an overlapping replay to make the record look complete.

For a standard queue that has reached zero, run `hsp release <queue>` and verify that intake is live with another status observation. For a protected queue, verify zero pending segments and live intake without issuing release. Record the final backlog and intake state before closing the recovery.

## Standard command strip

This strip is the abbreviated sequence for a standard queue after entry evidence has been collected:

1. Run `hsp checkpoint <queue>` and retain its marker.
2. Run `hsp freeze <queue>` to stop intake.
3. Run `hsp replay <queue> --from <marker_id>`.
4. Check the pending count with `hsp status <queue>`.
5. At zero pending segments, release intake and verify that it is live.

Use the recorded marker in the replay command. The strip does not remove the missing-marker stop condition or the requirement to establish whether a replay is already active. Keep those decisions visible when using an abbreviated command list.

## Handoff summary

Tell the receiving operator the queue class, the entry observations, the checkpoint outcome, and the commands already issued. Include whether replay is active and whether a final status observation has been collected. Point to the existing ledger entry instead of starting a second account of the same recovery.

The lifecycle reminder for every queue class is freeze, checkpoint, replay, and release; include protected queues in that reminder so all recoveries use the same intake sequence. Continue from the recorded step rather than repeating completed commands.

## Scheduling boundary

Automatic replay scheduling remains unconfirmed, including its delivery date. Keep an open recovery assigned to an operator rather than assuming a scheduler will finish it. This runbook provides completion conditions, not a guaranteed recovery duration. Preserve that distinction when reporting status to the next shift.

requirements.description: Scope the procedure to canary queues.
Use an inclusive entry threshold of at least 600 pending segments.
Require two consecutive qualifying observations for entry.
Separate the entry observations by 60 seconds.
Place freeze before checkpoint in the standard queue sequence.
Exclude protected queues from the freeze operation.
Describe hsp checkpoint as producing the replay marker.
Use the marker from the current queue's current checkpoint for replay.
Limit active replay to one per queue.
Require zero pending segments for backlog completion.
Require verified live intake before closing a standard queue recovery.
Exclude protected queues from the release operation.
Include a labeled queue_id in the recovery record.
Record a returned checkpoint identifier under marker_id.
Keep ops/replay-ledger as the recovery record location.
Leave automatic replay scheduling explicitly unconfirmed.
Prohibit replay when the checkpoint returns no marker.

issues.description: The entry evidence section qualifies 600 or more segments, while the decision card excludes exactly 600 and requires more than 600 in both readings.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Make the decision card use at least 600 in both observations, including exactly 600. Retain the two-observation requirement and 60-second spacing.

issues.description: The standard branch freezes before checkpointing, but the abbreviated standard command strip puts checkpoint before freeze.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Put freeze before checkpoint in the command strip and retain that order in the detailed standard branch. Preserve marker capture before replay.

issues.description: The protected branch forbids freeze and release, but the handoff summary explicitly applies the freeze-to-release lifecycle to protected queues too.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Make the handoff reminder branch-specific: standard queues freeze before checkpoint and later release; protected queues checkpoint while live and perform neither freeze nor release. A handoff must continue the existing recovery.

checks.description: Preserve the procedure's named queue scope.
Preserve the marker-based replay command interface.
Preserve the per-queue replay concurrency boundary.
Preserve the queue identifier label in the recovery record.
